title: Bring-Your-Own-SLOs 30-60-90 Collab Sprint Playbook
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This doc is a tactical playbook for running a 30-60-90 cross-functional engagement were calling "Bring-Your-Own-SLOs" (BYO-SLO). The objective: onboard feature teams to pragmatic, service-aligned SLOs, validate observability and alerting, and deliver repeatable SLO artifacts (SLO Card + runbook snippet + short canary experiment) so teams can ship with measurable reliability guardrails.

Context and why this is different:
- Weve run SLO workshops before; BYO-SLO flips the model: teams propose a candidate SLO for their service before the workshop, bringing real data and a hypothesis. The SRE role is to validate, instrument, and operationalize rather than dictate numbers.
- Focus is practical: a minimal set of things that must land by 30/60/90 days rather than a long, theoretical program.

Audience:
- Feature/product engineering teams (owners of the service)
- SRE reliability partners and on-call engineers
- Product and PM stakeholders
- Observability/Telemetry team (metrics, dashboards)

Success criteria (how we'll know this worked):
- By day 30: 80% of participating services have a published SLO Card draft and an agreed instrumentation plan (metrics & dashboards) assigned in JIRA.
- By day 60: 60% have automated alerts derived from SLO thresholds and a short canary run (synthetic or traffic-shadow) executed with results logged.
- By day 90: 50% have the SLO enforced in release gating (simple gate: block prod rollout if SLO errorbudget exhausted) and runbook + oncall handoff completed.

Scope and constraints:
- Target initially: 8 pilot services across product teams that represent a diversity of traffic patterns (sync API, async jobs, embeddings batch, streaming).
- We are not requiring full consumer-facing SLAs; these are internal SLOs tied to user-impacting signals.
- Default measurement window: rolling 28-day errorbudget; short-term testing windows (1d, 7d) for canaries.

30-60-90 timeline (high level):
- Days 0-30 (Discovery + Instrumentation): collection of team proposals, workshop 1 (validation), instrumentation tasks created, basic dashboards deployed.
- Days 31-60 (Alerting + Canary): alerts configured, canary experiments defined/executed, adjustments to SLO definitions.
- Days 61-90 (Gating + Handoff): rollout gating integrated into CI/CD for participating services, runbooks finalized, sign-off and transfer to steady-state SRE support.

Detailed week-by-week plan (actions and owners):
- Week 0 (prep): SRE lead (Aisha) publishes cohort invite, template SLO Card (fields below), and onboarding checklist. Observability lead (Liam) ensures metric names and doc examples are accessible.
- Week 1: Teams submit their candidate SLO & dataset link. Workshop 1 (2hr) co-run by SRE + Observability: validate signal, feasibility, and proposed threshold. Action: create JIRA epic per service with tasks (instrument metrics, dashboard, alert, canary).
- Week 2-4: Instrumentation sprint. Owners: feature team engineers implement metrics; SRE reviews PRs. Observability deploys dashboard template. Checkpoint meeting at day 21.
- Week 5-8: Alerting + Canary. SRE creates alert runbooks and designs lightweight canary plan (percent shadowing or synthetic probes). Execute canary, collect results, adjust thresholds.
- Week 9-12: CI gating + handoff. Integrate an SLO check in the deployment pipeline (blocking rule or advisory step). Final runbook, oncall paging tested. Close JIRA epic and record post-mortem/learnings.

SLO Card template (team should fill this before first workshop):
- Service name (short):
- Owner(s) + contact:
- User-facing impact (one sentence):
- Golden signal(s) chosen: latency / availability / correctness / throughput (select up to 2)
- Metric name and source (example: http_request_duration_seconds{route=/v1/generate} P50/P95):
- SLI definition (how metric maps to user success):
- SLO target (e.g., 99.5% success over 28 days):
- Error budget policy (what happens if exhausted):
- Canary test plan (short):
- Runbook summary (one paragraph):

Instrumentation checklist (minimal):
- Metric emitted at sufficient cardinality (team)
- Aggregation (service-level, not host-level) (Observability)
- Dashboard tile (P50/P95 and error rate/time series) (Observability)
- Alert rule (severity: P1/P2 mapping) (SRE)

Canary experiment ideas (pick one that fits the service):
- Shadow X% of real traffic to new model/router and compare success rate over 24h.
- Synthetic probe that exercises heavy path (every 3m for 48h) and measures end-to-end success.
- Batch job a/b run using production dataset subset and compare throughput/failure rates.

Risk matrix (quick view):
- Risk: Metric has low fidelity -> Mitigation: fallback to synthetic probes + tight rolling windows until fidelity improved.
- Risk: Alert spam during initial tuning -> Mitigation: use diagnostic severity flags and Mute window until stabilized.
- Risk: Teams lack capacity -> Mitigation: SRE + Observability provide 3h paired sessions each sprint week.

Communications and rituals:
- Weekly 30m sync (Aisha): progress updates, blockers, decisions logged in the shared Decisions doc.
- Biweekly demo (show-and-tell): teams demo dashboards and canary outputs.
- Emergency channel: #sre-byoslo-pilot in Slack for rapid escalations.

Decision log template (kept in the JIRA epic):
- Date | Decision | Rationale | Owner | Follow-up action

Metrics we will track for program health (team-level and program-level):
- Number of services with published SLO Card draft
- Time to first alert from cohort start
- Percent of canaries that pass within tolerance
- Number of alerts fired per service during tuning window
- Post-handoff ticket backlog for reliability bugs

Staffing and time estimates (per pilot service):
- Prep/validation: 3-6 engineer-hours (team + SRE review)
- Instrumentation: 1-2 engineer-days
- Alerting + runbook: 0.5-1 engineer-day + 2 SRE hours to review
- Canary execution and analysis: 1-2 engineer-days
- CI gating integration: 4-8 engineer-hours

Templates and artifacts to produce (deliverables):
- SLO Card (finalized) stored in Confluence (link anchored in JIRA epic)
- Minimal runbook (1 page) added to runbook repo
- Dashboard + alert rule in observability stack (grafana/tempo/omega) with IDs in JIRA
- Canary results log and decision capture

Open questions to resolve in kickoff:
- Which deployment pipelines can accept a blocking gate vs advisory check? (product infra)
- Are there budgeted paid synthetic probes we can run for external dependencies? (platform infra)
- How tightly do product managers want to couple SLO to feature launch timelines?

Next immediate actions (Today -> Day 7):
- Publish this playbook and invite pilot services (Aisha)
- Observability to share dashboard template and metric naming guidance (Liam)
- Product infra to confirm gating options and a contact (Sofia)
- Each pilot owner to submit SLO Card draft to the cohort folder (owners)

Notes and scratchpad (things we might add later):
- Consider a lightweight "SLO health badge" that displays pass/warn/fail in the service README.
- Build a small generator script to create baseline dashboards from the SLO Card metadata.
- Draft an internal FAQ about error budgets and escalation semantics (aim: 1 pager).

Appendix: sample short SLO Card (example service)
- Service name: embed-service
- Owners: Priya Menon, Omar Farouk
- Impact: downstream features rely on embedding latency; user waits for embeddings to start.
- Golden signals: P95 latency, error rate (timeout/5xx)
- SLI: fraction of requests with P95 latency < 800ms and 5xx rate < 0.5%
- SLO: 99% over a 28-day rolling window
- Error budget policy: advisory + rollback gate if budget exhausted for two consecutive 24h windows
- Canary: shadow 5% of traffic for 72h and compare latency distribution
- Runbook: page on high-5xx rate; immediate mitigation: revert most recent model/quantization or route to fallback instance.

End of playbook.

(If this pilot looks good we can scale to a quarterly BYO-SLO cohort cadence and bake artifacts into onboarding for new product teams.)
